Horizon-specific split conformal (MSCP) addresses the core challenge of multi-horizon prediction intervals in dependent time series by splitting training data per forecast horizon. This avoids violating exchangeability assumptions that invalidate standard conformal inference. The method uses finite-sample corrections via order statistics to define prediction intervals Γ_α(x_new) = [ŷ_new - q_{1-α}, ŷ_new + q_{1-α}]. Residuals serve as nonconformity scores, capturing temporal dynamics through lagged features. The Winkler interval score evaluates performance by balancing interval width and coverage accuracy. These primitives enable GSE to generate valid yet efficient intervals without assuming independence across time steps, crucial for practical forecasting applications.
